SHADOWFAX.why: Listed at ₹112.60, a 9% discount to the ₹124 issue price, then more than doubled. Q4 FY26 revenue rose 74% to ₹1,237 crore on higher e-commerce, quick-commerce and enterprise volumes, with a ₹56 crore profit; Q1 FY27 profit jumped eightfold to ₹65 crore and the shares hit a 52-week high of ₹246.80 (about +45% in three months). Some figures come from a syndicated article of limited reliability.
SHADOWFAX.outlook: Simply Wall St forecasts earnings growing 72% a year and revenue 24% a year, but with a modest return on equity near 12% in three years. Trailing P/E was above 100, so valuation prices in a lot. Risks: competition from Delhivery and XpressBees, fuel costs and volume slowdowns. No management guidance or analyst targets were found.

FRACTAL.why: Below the ₹900 issue price after a weak debut in February 2026 (opened at ₹876). The IPO was cut by over 40% (₹4,900 crore to ₹2,834 crore) on banker advice and employee demand was only 0.65x, in a market that was selling software and analytics names on fears that AI tools could disrupt them. A June article put it around ₹940, about 16% off a ₹1,118 high; FY26 revenue was about ₹3,362 crore with growth near 19%.
FRACTAL.outlook: That article calls the fall a pullback in a premium-valued AI listing, not a sign of business trouble. Other reasons cited: a P/E above peers (about 57x trailing) and promoter share pledging shortly after listing. No brokerage targets or company guidance were found; profitability figures varied across sources.

KISSHT.why: More than doubled the ₹171 issue price after listing at ₹191 (an 11.7% premium; IPO subscribed 9.5x). FY26 revenue from operations rose 63% to ₹2,179 crore, Q4 FY26 profit rose 52%, and Q1 FY27 total income rose 45% to ₹677 crore. It runs a data-first, machine-learning credit and collections model and added loans against property.
KISSHT.outlook: No analyst consensus or management guidance for 2026 was found. Valuation looks full on some screens (trailing P/E near 69) and profitability measures varied by source. As a lender, asset quality and funding costs are the main things to watch in later results.

TURTLEMINT.why: Down about 55% since the June 2026 listing at a discount (opened ₹134.90 against ₹152 issue price; IPO subscribed only about 1.2x) because it is still loss-making. The sharpest drop came in September 2026 when IRDAI proposed changes to insurance distribution rules, raising fear for commission income: the shares fell from about ₹136 to ₹109 and then toward ₹70 within days (down 20% in the week to 25 September).
TURTLEMINT.outlook: The main near-term risk is the final form and timing of the IRDAI commission proposal; a peer was hit too. Profitability is unproven and investors want a clear path to it. IPO money goes to technology, marketing, working capital and acquisitions. The regulatory link is the usual explanation, not a confirmed one.

CSM.why: Weak from day one: listed flat at ₹113 on 2 July 2026 (IPO subscribed only about 1.4x) and immediately hit the 5% lower circuit. The sources describe valuation worries: post-listing P/E near 30x against a listed-peer average of about 13.8x. It is a GovTech and IT services firm in 12 countries with an order book of ₹357.6 crore (March 2026).
CSM.outlook: No analyst targets or management guidance were found. One analysis says high growth expectations are already priced in and investors want stronger execution before paying a premium. Check its first listed-company quarterly results.

XTRANET.why: Listed at ₹136 (7% above the ₹127 issue price; IPO subscribed 12.2x, all fresh issue) and the pop faded within hours. The sources found cover only listing day, so the reason it later climbed to more than double the issue price was not found. Analysts then described a fair valuation (P/E 17.5x against a peer average near 39.8x) and warned of dependence on government orders.
XTRANET.outlook: No post-listing results, analyst targets or guidance were found. With the stock now about 2.4x the issue price, check its first quarterly results to see whether fundamentals support the move. This is the least-explained rally in the list.

SHIPROCKET.why: Listed 19 August 2026 at ₹131, 35% above the ₹97 issue price, on a 99x subscribed IPO with 13 mutual funds in the anchor book. It rose to about ₹156-157 in the first days, fell to about ₹117-120 by late September (as the anchor lock-in ended on 16 September), then rebounded about 6% on 6 October with no company trigger. FY26 revenue was about ₹2,053 crore with a loss near ₹35 crore.
SHIPROCKET.outlook: The rest of the lock-in ends 15 November 2026, a possible selling point. Analysts frame the case around reaching EBITDA profitability and positive cash flow; EV to revenue rose from 3.6x to 4.8x at listing. Risks: logistics and e-commerce regulation and reliance on third-party couriers. First listed results were due.

TEMPSENS.why: Listed 28 August 2026 at ₹634, a 111% premium to the ₹300 issue price, on a heavily oversubscribed IPO (reported at 184x) and a surging grey market premium. FY26 revenue rose 17.5% to ₹444.9 crore. It makes temperature sensors, industrial heaters and engineered cables. Of the ₹650 crore issue only ₹95 crore was fresh capital; ₹555 crore was an offer for sale by existing holders.
TEMPSENS.outlook: No analyst ratings or post-listing results were found. The price roughly doubled on listing-day demand rather than a change in results, so first quarterly results as a listed company will test it. Because most proceeds went to selling shareholders, the company itself raised little.

ESDS.why: Listed 4 September 2026 at ₹757, 76% above the ₹429 issue price, after the IPO was subscribed about 143x (QIBs 275x), then hit the 20% upper circuit in each of its first sessions, reaching about ₹1,675 within five sessions and a high of ₹1,859 on 24 September. Coverage ties the rally to AI and cloud infrastructure exposure; ₹576 crore of the ₹720 crore raise goes to cloud computing equipment.
ESDS.outlook: Commentary is positive on long-term cloud and data-centre demand but warns valuation has moved ahead of fundamentals and much of the near-term growth may be priced in. No analyst targets, post-listing results or guidance were found. Large post-IPO runs are usually volatile.
